summary: Anthropic released Claude Opus 4.7, an upgrade to Opus 4.6 with improved coding, vision, agentic reliability and a new effort-control setting, at unchanged pricing.

mechanisms.reason: The document describes measurable capability gains over the prior model across coding, vision, document reasoning and long-horizon agentic tasks.
mechanisms.quote: Opus 4.7 is a notable improvement on Opus 4.6 in advanced software engineering, with particular gains on the most difficult tasks.

mechanisms.reason: Multiple partner testimonials describe Opus 4.7 enabling longer, more autonomous multi-step agentic work with less human supervision.
mechanisms.quote: Claude Opus 4.7 takes long-horizon autonomy to a new level in Devin. It works coherently for hours, pushes through hard problems rather than giving up, and unlocks a class of deep investigation work we couldn't reliably run before.

mechanisms.reason: The model reasons more at higher effort levels and produces more output tokens, indicating higher per-task compute consumption.
mechanisms.quote: Opus 4.7 thinks more at higher effort levels, particularly on later turns in agentic settings. This improves its reliability on hard problems, but it does mean it produces more output tokens.

mechanisms.reason: Higher-resolution image support and an updated tokenizer that maps input to more tokens increase per-request context and memory load.
mechanisms.quote: it can accept images up to 2,576 pixels on the long edge (~3.75 megapixels), more than three times as many as prior Claude models
